identity.name: Dograh
identity.one_liner: Open-source self-hosted voice AI platform with visual workflows, MCP support, BYOK model routing, and telephony.
identity.short_description: Dograh is an open-source voice AI platform positioned as a self-hosted alternative to hosted voice-agent products. It supports on-premise deployment, BYOK model choices, speech-to-speech or modular LLM/STT/TTS workflows, visual workflow building, MCP-native integrations, and telephony support.

positioning.why_it_matters: Voice agents are becoming a practical bot category, but many teams need control over hosting, telephony, and model providers. Dograh gives voice-agent builders an open-source platform to evaluate.
best_for: Developers comparing alternatives to hosted voice AI platforms
Operators who need telephony workflows with model-provider flexibility
not_for: Teams that do not want to operate voice, telephony, or speech infrastructure

core_strengths.title: Self-hosted voice platform
core_strengths.description: Dograh is positioned for on-premise and self-hosted voice AI workflows.
core_strengths.why_it_matters: Voice agents often touch customer data and telephony systems, so deployment control matters.

core_strengths.title: BYOK model routing
core_strengths.description: The project supports bring-your-own-key across speech-to-speech or modular LLM, STT, and TTS flows.
core_strengths.why_it_matters: Voice teams can compare providers without locking the whole stack to one vendor.

core_strengths.title: Visual workflows and MCP
core_strengths.description: Dograh includes a visual workflow builder and MCP-native positioning.
core_strengths.why_it_matters: Voice agents need operational flows, integrations, and tool access beyond a single prompt.

seo_article.intro: Dograh is an open-source self-hosted voice AI platform.
seo_article.what_it_is: It combines voice-agent workflows, telephony, BYOK model routing, visual workflow building, and MCP-native integrations.
seo_article.why_it_matters: Voice agents are moving into real customer workflows, where hosting, latency, provider choice, and auditability all matter.
seo_article.how_it_works: Start with a low-risk voice workflow, test speech recognition and handoff behavior, and evaluate deployment requirements before production use.

faq.question: Is Dograh open source?
faq.answer: Yes. The GitHub repository is listed under the BSD-2-Clause license.

faq.question: Who should evaluate Dograh?
faq.answer: Teams building self-hosted voice agents or comparing open alternatives to hosted voice AI platforms should evaluate it.
